questions.title: Which month of 2026 will have the highest ICE arrest total in the data publicly available by August 26, 2026?
questions.background: U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) carries out arrests as part of federal immigration enforcement.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Use government data supplied by ICE, as reported by The Associated Press. Resolution Date : Resolve to the calendar month of 2026 with the largest arrest total among the months covered by the latest ICE monthly figures publicly available by August 26, 2026. Accepted Answer Format : Answer with the month name only.
questions.current_reasoning: Major 2026-07-20/22 breaking data release completely overturns the prior blackout thesis: on Monday July 20, ICE ended its 3+ month reporting hiatus (since April 9) and published official Detention Management statistics covering through July 11, 2026 (reported July 21-22 by CBS News, The Guardian, ABC News, Stateline, Denver Gazette, Deseret News, and EFE). Two decisive facts follow: (1) June 2026 logged 43,138 total arrests/detention book-ins (39,563 ICE + 3,575 CBP, averaging 1,438/day) — officially confirmed as the highest monthly total of Trump's second term, surpassing December 2025 (42,107) and every month January-May 2026, collapsing January from 0.54 to 0.04 (retained only for small edge-case risk that AP cites an alternate ICE-only DDP FOIA series still ending March 11); (2) July 1-11 surged even higher to 1,593 arrests/day (~17,523 total; 16,213 ICE-only), putting 31-day July on track for ~49,000-50,000 arrests (needing only ~1,281/day over July 12-31 to beat June, while Trump immediately reversed the brief July 15 vehicle-stop pause and DHS Sec Mullin boasted July 17 of hitting single-day records daily). Conditional on full-month July figures being published by August 26 (~70% likely given ICE just resumed publishing with a 9-day lag and has 37 days / ~2-3 biweekly cycles before Aug 26), July beats June ~89% of the time -> July 0.62. June rises to 0.32 to reflect ~25-30% risk that ICE slips into another reporting delay past Aug 26 (or only covers partial July) plus ~10% conditional chance of a late-July operational drop; August holds 0.01 (1% residual).

questions.title: Who will win the men's singles title at the 2026 Mubadala DC Open?
questions.background: The Mubadala DC Open is a professional tennis tournament in Washington, D.C. Its men's singles competition is part of the ATP Tour.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : The official ATP results for the 2026 Mubadala DC Open. Resolution Condition : Resolve to the player officially recorded as the men's singles champion once the tournament final is completed and the result is confirmed. Accepted Answer Format : The champion's full name.
questions.current_reasoning: Major field and bracket overhaul on July 22-25: two of our previous top five (Felix Auger-Aliassime and Daniil Medvedev) withdrew on July 22, leaving only three healthy Top-10 players in the 32-man main draw released July 25. The draw is heavily lopsided: No. 2 seed Ben Shelton (WC, World No. 5, 2x DC semifinalist, rested after early Wimbledon exit) is the lone healthy Top-10 star in a much softer bottom half (opening vs Ethan Quinn, R2 vs Humbert/Q, QF vs Tiafoe, SF vs returning-from-injury Musetti / Fils / Jodar), promoting him to #1 favorite (0.19). The stacked top half pits No. 1 seed and defending champion Alex de Minaur against nemesis and fresh Gstaad champion Stefanos Tsitsipas in R1 (1-12 H2H!), with Jakub Mensik/Brandon Nakashima looming in QF and Taylor Fritz, Tommy Paul, Learner Tien, and Jack Draper all packed into Quarter 2 for the SF. Fritz rises to 0.16 (cleanest top-half favorite), de Minaur holds near 0.14 despite the withdrawals due to the brutal Tsitsipas R1 trap and stacked top half, Frances Tiafoe (0.07, home crowd, 3-0 in 2026 vs R1 foe Atmane, softer bottom half) and Jakub Mensik (0.065, seeded power server in Q1 who benefits if Tsitsipas upsets de Minaur) enter the top five; 37.5% remains on Learner Tien, Arthur Fils, Tommy Paul, Lorenzo Musetti, Jack Draper, Tsitsipas, Rafael Jodar, and the rest of the 32-man draw.

questions.current_reasoning: The official 28-player WTA Mubadala DC Open draw was released on July 25 with all five of our top contenders confirmed and no further top-8 withdrawals. The bracket strongly favors top seed Jessica Pegula (up 0.19 -> 0.22): she has a R1 bye (only 4 wins needed) in a noticeably softer top half alongside No. 4 Diana Shnaider (bye, 0.085), No. 5 Anna Kalinskaya, and No. 6 Madison Keys (0.06, no bye, tough R1 vs 2022 DC champ Liudmila Samsonova, and 0-2 vs Pegula in 2026). Remaining 41% covers Kalinskaya, Zheng Qinwen, Fernandez, Navarro, Tauson, Samsonova, Eala, and the rest of the field.

questions.title: Which club will Mohamed Salah join first after leaving Liverpool at the end of the 2025–26 season?
questions.background: Mohamed Salah has announced that he will leave Liverpool at the end of the season.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : An official announcement from Salah or his new club, or reliable news reporting confirming a completed signing. Resolution Condition : Resolve to the first club with which Salah signs a senior playing contract following his departure from Liverpool at the end of the 2025–26 season. Transfer speculation, negotiations, and trial appearances do not qualify. Accepted Answer Format : The name of the club.
questions.current_reasoning: 2026-07-25/26 update (Juvefc citing Corriere dello Sport & Turkish Tier-1 journalist Yagiz Sabuncuoglu, alongside Liverpool.com citing Nicolo Schira): Sabuncuoglu independently reports that the main sticking point that previously stalled Besiktas's deal—agent Ramy Abbas's €7.5m (35%) commission demand—has been reduced to a workable figure, clearing the path for an announcement on a reported €10m-€12m/yr contract. Corriere dello Sport adds Besiktas are already pitching Salah's imminent arrival to recruit free-agent striker Dusan Vlahovic (while noting Juventus balked at matching Vlahovic's €8m/yr wage, making a costly Juve bid for Salah less likely). With zero rival club reporting an advanced agreement and Salah a free agent requiring no transfer fee, lifting Besiktas from 0.49 -> 0.55 (disciplined cap at 0.55 pending official signing/announcement given prior Ramy Abbas friction), and trimming Al-Hilal (0.10 -> 0.09), Al-Ahli (0.10 -> 0.09), Al-Ittihad (0.08 -> 0.07), and Juventus (0.07 -> 0.05), leaving 15% residual for MLS (Sporting KC, San Diego FC) and other clubs.

questions.title: Who will win Michigan’s 2026 Democratic primary for U.S. Senate?
questions.background: Michigan will elect a U.S. senator in November 2026. The Democratic primary will determine the party’s nominee for that election.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Results from Michigan election authorities or unambiguous reporting by major news organizations identifying the winner of Michigan’s 2026 Democratic primary for U.S. Senate. Resolution Date : Resolve when the winner of the primary, scheduled for August 4, 2026, is publicly established. Accepted Answer Format : The winning candidate’s name.
questions.current_reasoning: Blockbuster 2026-07-24 endorsement: Michigan Gov. Gretchen Whitmer officially endorsed Rep. Haley Stevens one day before early in-person voting opens (July 25) and 11 days before the Aug 4 primary (AP, NBC News, CBS News, Detroit Free Press, Decision Desk HQ). Whitmer holds >80% approval among Michigan Democrats (having defeated El-Sayed by 22 points in 2018), and the July Detroit News/WDIV Glengariff poll specifically found 50% of undecided primary voters said a Whitmer endorsement would make them more likely to back a candidate. Non-partisan polls already gave Stevens an edge (Glengariff 48-41, Tavern 42-41) before both Sen. Gary Peters' (July 13) and Whitmer's (July 24) endorsements. Offsetting this, Decision Desk HQ's July 24 primary average still puts El-Sayed up 47-41 (boosted by two pro-El-Sayed sponsored polls: Tulchin 56-40 and Data for Progress 54-41), El-Sayed added endorsements from Sen. Elizabeth Warren (July 21) and 314 Action PAC (July 22), nearly a month of absentee ballots have already been cast, and liquid prediction markets had El-Sayed ~66% pre-Whitmer. Recalibrating sharply from 0.63/0.37 to a virtual toss-up: Abdul El-Sayed 0.51, Haley Stevens 0.49.
